title: gh-cli
description: The official GitHub CLI — manage repositories, issues, pull requests, releases, and GitHub Actions from your terminal.

Getting Started.Getting Started:
`gh` is GitHub's official command line tool. It wraps the GitHub API so you can create repos, open pull requests, review code, manage issues, and trigger workflows without leaving your terminal.

## Install

**Arch Linux**

```bash
sudo pacman -S github-cli
```

**Other platforms**

```bash
# macOS
brew install gh

# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt install gh

# Windows (winget)
winget install --id GitHub.cli
```

See the [official installation docs](https://github.com/cli/cli#installation) for more package managers.

## Authenticate

```bash
gh auth login
```

This walks you through an interactive setup: choose `GitHub.com` (or your GitHub Enterprise host), choose `HTTPS` or `SSH` as your preferred protocol, and authenticate via browser or a personal access token.

Check your login status any time:

```bash
gh auth status
```

## Verify it works

```bash
gh --version
gh repo list
```

If `gh repo list` prints repositories you own or have access to, you're authenticated and ready to go.

## Shell completion

```bash
# bash
gh completion -s bash | sudo tee /etc/bash_completion.d/gh

# zsh
gh completion -s zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_gh"
```

Next: [Configuration](/gh-cli/0.0.0/getting-started/configuration/) to set your defaults, or jump straight into [Essential Commands](/gh-cli/0.0.0/essential-commands/overview/).
Getting Started.Configuration:
`gh` stores its configuration in `~/.config/gh/config.yml` on Linux.

## View and set config values

```bash
gh config list
gh config get editor
gh config set editor "nvim"
gh config set git_protocol ssh
```

Common keys:

| Key | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor` | Editor used for commit messages, PR bodies, etc. | `nvim`, `code --wait` |
| `git_protocol` | Protocol used when cloning (`https` or `ssh`) | `ssh` |
| `prompt` | Whether `gh` asks interactive questions | `enabled` / `disabled` |
| `pager` | Pager for long output | `less`, `bat` |

## Default repository

When you run `gh` commands outside a git repo, or when a folder has multiple possible remotes, `gh` may ask which repository to use. Set a default explicitly from inside a repo:

```bash
gh repo set-default owner/repo
```

## Aliases

`gh` supports custom command aliases, similar to `git alias`:

```bash
gh alias set prs 'pr list --author "@me"'
gh alias set co 'pr checkout'
gh alias list
```

Now `gh prs` lists your open pull requests, and `gh co 42` checks out PR #42.

## Multiple accounts / hosts

```bash
gh auth login --hostname github.example.com
gh auth switch
```

Useful if you work with both `github.com` and a GitHub Enterprise instance.

Essential Commands.Repositories:
Commands for creating, cloning, and inspecting repositories.

## Create a repository

```bash
gh repo create my-project --public --clone
gh repo create my-project --private --source=. --remote=origin
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--public` / `--private` / `--internal` | Visibility |
| `--clone` | Clone the new repo locally after creating it |
| `--source=.` | Use the current directory as the repo source |
| `--remote=origin` | Name for the git remote when using `--source` |
| `--description "..."` | Set the repo description |
| `--gitignore Dart` | Seed a `.gitignore` template |
| `--license MIT` | Seed a license file |

## Clone a repository

```bash
gh repo clone owner/repo
gh repo clone owner/repo -- --depth=1
```

Anything after `--` is passed straight through to `git clone`.

## Fork a repository

```bash
gh repo fork owner/repo --clone
```

Forks the repo into your account and clones it, wiring up `upstream` as a remote automatically.

## View repository info

```bash
gh repo view
gh repo view owner/repo
gh repo view owner/repo --web
```

`--web` opens the repo in your browser instead of printing to the terminal.

## List repositories

```bash
gh repo list
gh repo list my-org --limit 50
```

## Delete / rename / archive

```bash
gh repo delete owner/repo
gh repo rename new-name
gh repo archive owner/repo
```

Essential Commands.Issues:
Commands for creating and managing issues.

## Create an issue

```bash
gh issue create --title "Bug: crash on startup" --body "Steps to reproduce..."
gh issue create --title "Bug" --body "..." --label bug --assignee @me
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--title` | Issue title |
| `--body` | Issue body (or `--body-file file.md`) |
| `--label` | Comma-separated labels |
| `--assignee` | Comma-separated usernames, or `@me` |
| `--milestone` | Attach to a milestone |
| `--web` | Open the "new issue" form in your browser instead |

## List issues

```bash
gh issue list
gh issue list --state open --label bug
gh issue list --author "@me"
gh issue list --assignee "@me"
```

## View an issue

```bash
gh issue view 42
gh issue view 42 --web
gh issue view 42 --comments
```

## Comment on / close / reopen

```bash
gh issue comment 42 --body "Fixed in #45"
gh issue close 42
gh issue reopen 42
```

## Edit

```bash
gh issue edit 42 --add-label "priority-high" --add-assignee octocat
```

Essential Commands.Pull Requests:
The most-used part of `gh` day to day: creating, reviewing, and merging pull requests without leaving the terminal.

## Create a pull request

```bash
gh pr create --title "Add retry logic" --body "Closes #12" --base main
gh pr create --fill
gh pr create --draft
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--title` / `--body` | PR title and description |
| `--base` | Target branch (defaults to the repo's default branch) |
| `--head` | Source branch (defaults to current branch) |
| `--fill` | Auto-fill title/body from the branch's commits |
| `--draft` | Open as a draft PR |
| `--reviewer` | Request reviewers, comma-separated |
| `--label` | Add labels |
| `--web` | Open the "new PR" form in your browser instead |

## List and view

```bash
gh pr list
gh pr list --author "@me"
gh pr view 42
gh pr view 42 --web
gh pr view --json state,mergeable,reviewDecision
```

## Checkout a PR locally

```bash
gh pr checkout 42
```

Fetches and checks out the PR's branch — great for testing someone else's change before approving it.

## Check status

```bash
gh pr status
gh pr checks 42
```

`gh pr status` shows a summary: PRs you opened, PRs requesting your review, and PRs assigned to you.

## Review

```bash
gh pr review 42 --approve
gh pr review 42 --request-changes --body "Please add a test"
gh pr review 42 --comment --body "Looks good overall"
```

## Diff

```bash
gh pr diff 42
```

## Merge

```bash
gh pr merge 42 --squash --delete-branch
gh pr merge 42 --merge
gh pr merge 42 --rebase
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--squash` | Squash all commits into one |
| `--merge` | Standard merge commit |
| `--rebase` | Rebase and merge |
| `--delete-branch` | Delete the branch after merging |
| `--auto` | Enable auto-merge (merges once checks pass) |

Essential Commands.Releases:
Commands for cutting releases and managing their assets.

## Create a release

```bash
gh release create v1.0.0 --title "v1.0.0" --notes "Initial release"
gh release create v1.0.0 --generate-notes
gh release create v1.0.0 ./build/app.tar.gz
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--title` | Release title |
| `--notes` / `--notes-file` | Release notes |
| `--generate-notes` | Auto-generate notes from merged PRs |
| `--draft` | Create as a draft |
| `--prerelease` | Mark as a pre-release |
| trailing file args | Upload these files as release assets |

## List and view

```bash
gh release list
gh release view v1.0.0
```

## Download assets

```bash
gh release download v1.0.0
gh release download v1.0.0 --pattern "*.tar.gz"
```

## Upload additional assets / delete

```bash
gh release upload v1.0.0 ./checksums.txt
gh release delete v1.0.0
```

Essential Commands.GitHub Actions:
Inspect and trigger CI workflows without opening the Actions tab in your browser.

## List workflows and runs

```bash
gh workflow list
gh run list
gh run list --workflow=ci.yml
```

## View a run

```bash
gh run view
gh run view 123456789
gh run view 123456789 --log
```

`gh run view` with no ID shows the most recent run.

## Watch a run live

```bash
gh run watch
```

Streams status updates until the run finishes — useful right after a push.

## Trigger a workflow manually

```bash
gh workflow run ci.yml
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref feature-branch -f environment=staging
```

`-f key=value` passes `workflow_dispatch` inputs.

## Re-run / cancel

```bash
gh run rerun 123456789
gh run rerun 123456789 --failed
gh run cancel 123456789
```

Next: [Gists & Search](/gh-cli/0.0.0/essential-commands/gists-&-search/).
Essential Commands.Gists & Search:
Smaller but handy tools: sharing snippets, searching GitHub, and calling the raw API.

## Gists

```bash
gh gist create script.dart
gh gist create script.dart --public
gh gist list
gh gist view <gist-id>
```

## Search

```bash
gh search repos "http client" --language=dart
gh search issues "is:open label:bug" --repo owner/repo
gh search prs "is:open review:required" --owner my-org
```

`gh search` mirrors GitHub's search qualifiers (`is:`, `label:`, `author:`, etc.).

## Raw API access

For anything not covered by a dedicated subcommand, `gh api` calls the GitHub REST or GraphQL API directly, using your existing `gh` authentication:

```bash
gh api repos/owner/repo
gh api repos/owner/repo/issues --paginate
gh api graphql -f query='query { viewer { login } }'
```

This is the escape hatch: if a feature exists in the GitHub API but not as a friendly `gh` subcommand, `gh api` reaches it.

Learn by Using.1. Starting the Project:
We're building `reqly`, a small Dart HTTP client. Let's get it onto GitHub.

## Scaffold the project locally

```bash
mkdir reqly && cd reqly
dart create --template=package .
```

## Create the GitHub repository

Instead of creating the repo on github.com and cloning it, we create it *from* the folder we already have, using `--source`:

```bash
gh repo create reqly --public --source=. --remote=origin --description "A minimal HTTP client for Dart with retries built in."
```

`gh` creates `psdk/reqly` on GitHub, adds it as the `origin` remote, and leaves your local files untouched.

## First push

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git push -u origin main
```

## Confirm it worked

```bash
gh repo view
```

```text
psdk/reqly
A minimal HTTP client for Dart with retries built in.

...
```

`gh repo view` with no arguments always refers to the repo tied to your current directory — you'll use this constantly to sanity-check "am I even looking at the right repo."

Next: [Tracking Work with Issues](/gh-cli/0.0.0/learn-by-using/2.-tracking-work-with-issues/).
Learn by Using.2. Tracking Work with Issues:
Before writing more code, let's plan the next few pieces of work as issues — this is normal even for a solo project, since it gives you a changelog of *intent*, not just commits.

## File a few issues

```bash
gh issue create --title "Add retry logic for failed requests" \
  --body "Requests that fail with a 5xx should retry up to 3 times with backoff." \
  --label enhancement

gh issue create --title "Support custom timeout" \
  --body "Allow passing a Duration timeout to Reqly()." \
  --label enhancement

gh issue create --title "Document HTTP/2 support status" \
  --body "README should be explicit about whether HTTP/2 is supported." \
  --label documentation
```

Each `gh issue create` prints the new issue's URL, e.g. `https://github.com/psdk/reqly/issues/1`.

## Check what's open

```bash
gh issue list
```

```text
Showing 3 of 3 open issues in psdk/reqly

#3  Document HTTP/2 support status       documentation
#2  Support custom timeout               enhancement
#1  Add retry logic for failed requests  enhancement
```

## Filter by label

```bash
gh issue list --label enhancement
```

## Pick one to work on and assign yourself

```bash
gh issue edit 1 --add-assignee @me
gh issue view 1
```

We'll work on issue #1 — retry logic — next.

Next: [Branching and Opening a PR](/gh-cli/0.0.0/learn-by-using/3.-branching-and-opening-a-pr/).
Learn by Using.3. Branching and Opening a PR:
Time to actually write the retry logic from issue #1, and open a pull request for it — even solo, PRs give you CI checks and a clean history before merging to `main`.

## Create a branch and make changes

```bash
git checkout -b retry-logic
# ...edit lib/src/reqly_base.dart...
git add .
git commit -m "Add retry logic with exponential backoff"
git push -u origin retry-logic
```

## Open the pull request

```bash
gh pr create --title "Add retry logic" \
  --body "Closes #1. Retries failed requests up to 3 times with exponential backoff." \
  --base main
```

Using `Closes #1` in the body links the PR to the issue — GitHub will auto-close issue #1 when this PR merges.

If you're not ready for eyes on it yet:

```bash
gh pr create --draft --fill
```

`--fill` saves you typing a title/body by reusing your branch's commit messages.

## Confirm it's there

```bash
gh pr status
```

```text
Relevant pull requests in psdk/reqly

Current branch
  #4  Add retry logic [retry-logic]

Created by you
  #4  Add retry logic [retry-logic]

Requesting a code review from you
  You have no pull requests to review
```

## Keep working on the branch

Push more commits as normal — the PR updates automatically:

```bash
# ...more edits...
git add .
git commit -m "Add test for backoff timing"
git push
```

Next: [Reviewing and Merging](/gh-cli/0.0.0/learn-by-using/4.-reviewing-and-merging/).
Learn by Using.4. Reviewing and Merging:
The PR is open and CI is running. Let's check its status, review it, and merge.

## Check CI status

```bash
gh pr checks 4
```

```text
All checks were successful
0 cancelled, 0 failing, 2 successful, 0 skipped, 0 pending

NAME       DESCRIPTION            ELAPSED  URL
test       test / dart (pull_..)  38s      https://github.com/...
analyze    analyze / dart (pull.)  12s      https://github.com/...
```

If something's still running, watch it live:

```bash
gh run watch
```

## Review the diff before merging

```bash
gh pr diff 4
```

This prints the full unified diff right in the terminal — handy for a final read before you approve.

## Request a review (team project) or self-review (solo project)

```bash
gh pr review 4 --approve --body "Backoff logic looks correct, tests pass."
```

On a team, you'd instead do:

```bash
gh pr create --reviewer octocat --title "..." --body "..."
# or, on an existing PR:
gh pr edit 4 --add-reviewer octocat
```

## Take it out of draft, if needed

```bash
gh pr ready 4
```

## Merge

```bash
gh pr merge 4 --squash --delete-branch
```

```text
✓ Squashed and merged pull request #4 (Add retry logic)
✓ Deleted branch retry-logic and switched to branch main
```

Because the PR body said `Closes #1`, issue #1 is now closed automatically — check it:

```bash
gh issue view 1
```

## Sync your local main

```bash
git pull
```

Next: [Cutting a Release](/gh-cli/0.0.0/learn-by-using/5.-cutting-a-release/).
Learn by Using.5. Cutting a Release:
A few PRs later (support for custom timeouts, docs), `main` is in good shape. Time to cut `v1.0.0`.

## Tag and push

```bash
git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0
```

## Create the release from the tag

```bash
gh release create v1.0.0 --title "v1.0.0" --generate-notes
```

`--generate-notes` builds release notes automatically from the PRs merged since the last release (or since the beginning of the repo, for the first one) — no changelog file required.

## Check it

```bash
gh release view v1.0.0
```

```text
v1.0.0
psdk released this

## What's Changed
* Add retry logic by @psdk in #4
* Support custom timeout by @psdk in #5
* Document HTTP/2 support status by @psdk in #6

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/psdk/reqly/commits/v1.0.0
```

## Attach a build artifact (optional)

If your project produces a distributable file:

```bash
gh release upload v1.0.0 ./dist/reqly.tar.gz
```

## List all releases later

```bash
gh release list
```

Learn by Using.6. Daily Driving gh:
`reqly` is live with a tagged release. From here, most of your `gh` usage becomes short, habitual commands rather than the full workflow above. This page is a quick-reference for that daily rhythm.

## Starting your day

```bash
gh pr status      # what needs my attention?
gh issue list --assignee @me
```

## Starting a new piece of work

```bash
gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."
git checkout -b my-branch
# work, commit
git push -u origin my-branch
gh pr create --fill
```

## Checking someone else's PR

```bash
gh pr checkout 12
# test it locally
gh pr review 12 --approve
```

## Quick status checks

```bash
gh repo view                 # am I in the right repo?
gh pr view                   # status of the PR for my current branch
gh run list --limit 5        # recent CI runs
```

## Using aliases to shortcut all of this

Set these once (see [Configuration](/gh-cli/0.0.0/getting-started/configuration/)):

```bash
gh alias set prs 'pr list --author "@me"'
gh alias set myissues 'issue list --assignee "@me"'
gh alias set co 'pr checkout'
```

Now your morning routine is just:

```bash
gh prs
gh myissues
```

## When gh doesn't have a subcommand for it

Reach for `gh api` — see [Gists & Search](/gh-cli/0.0.0/essential-commands/gists-&-search/) for details:

```bash
gh api repos/psdk/reqly/traffic/views
```

That's the full loop: plan with issues, branch, open a PR, review, merge, release — then repeat, faster each time.

Project.FAQ:
### Does gh replace git?

No. `gh` complements `git` — you still use `git` for commits, branches, and local history. `gh` handles the GitHub-specific parts: repos, issues, PRs, releases, and Actions.

### Can I use gh with GitHub Enterprise?

Yes:

```bash
gh auth login --hostname github.example.com
```

### How do I use gh in a script non-interactively?

Pass flags instead of relying on prompts, and use `GH_TOKEN` for auth in CI:

```bash
GH_TOKEN=$MY_TOKEN gh pr create --title "..." --body "..." --base main
```

### Where's the config file on Arch Linux?

`~/.config/gh/config.yml` — see [Configuration](/gh-cli/0.0.0/getting-started/configuration/).

### How do I get JSON output for scripting?

Most commands support `--json` with a field list, often paired with `--jq`:

```bash
gh pr list --json number,title,author --jq '.[].title'
```
